=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:296-297, 302 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The sed patterns on lines 296-297 and the grep on line 302 match `^[[:space:]]*<!-- check-failure-triage:gen=...` at the start of any line, including lines inside a fenced Markdown code block. A source issue that is NOT a triage issue but contains a fenced example like `<!-- check-failure-triage:gen=3 -->` on a line-start inside a triple-backtick block causes `PGEN=3`, the script enters the `if` branch (line 298), increments the generation to 4, and inherits the lineage — instead of entering the `elif` branch at line 302 and starting a new generation-1 lineage. The lineage-cap guard at line 345 then escalates the PR before any triage issue is filed.
  WHY: The script's markers are always at the very top of the body (first 4 lines, validated later at lines 640+), but `^[[:space:]]*` alone cannot distinguish issue-top metadata from fenced-code-block content. A non-triage source issue that documents the marker format in a code block triggers incorrect lineage inheritance and premature escalation.
- changelog.d/claude-elegant-mendel-triage-lineage-gen1.md:line 10 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The changelog fragment states "Tests added | 3 (`CheckFailureTriageLineageTests` ...)". The original PR added 4 test methods (no-marker, prose-marker, increment, malformed). The first autofix added the prose-marker-as-separate-method, and the current (second) autofix last-run diff added `test_source_issue_mentioning_numeric_marker_inline_starts_generation_one`, bringing the total to 5. The count is stale.
  WHY: No runtime impact. The changelog is user-facing; operators and contributors reading it see a miscount.

- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:296–297, with the fallback check at 302 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Line-leading markers inside fenced Markdown code blocks are treated as real lineage metadata; the parser does not distinguish examples from the generated marker header.

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:Lines 296-297 (the PGEN/PROOT sed patterns) and the elif at line 303 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The line-leading sed pattern `^[[:space:]]*<!-- ${MARKER_PREFIX}gen=` also matches marker text inside fenced Markdown code blocks. A non-triage source issue whose body contains a fenced example such as ````\n<!-- check-failure-triage:gen=3 -->\n```` at the start of a line would set PGEN=3, causing the first branch to increment to generation 4 instead of starting at generation 1. The elif guard at line 303 uses the same pattern, so a fenced non-numeric example like `<!-- check-failure-triage:gen=abc -->` would also bypass the generation-1 path and hit the `parent_generation_missing_or_malformed` error.
  WHY: For non-triage source issues (the case this PR fixes), the body is pipeline-generated and unlikely to contain fenced triage-marker examples today. But the parser has no fence-awareness, so if a model-written heal or orchestrator issue ever quotes a marker in a fenced block, the lineage generation would be set from the example rather than starting fresh. The inline-backtick case is handled (tested), but the fenced-code-block case is not.
- changelog.d/claude-elegant-mendel-triage-lineage-gen1.md:Line 10 (`| Tests added | 3 |`) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The changelog fragment states "Tests added | 3" but `CheckFailureTriageLineageTests` contains 5 test methods: `test_source_issue_without_triage_marker_starts_generation_one`, `test_source_issue_mentioning_marker_in_prose_starts_generation_one`, `test_source_issue_mentioning_numeric_marker_inline_starts_generation_one`, `test_source_issue_with_triage_marker_increments_generation`, and `test_source_issue_with_malformed_triage_marker_still_fails`.
  WHY: No runtime impact. The changelog is a user-facing document; an incorrect count misleads operators and contributors reading the fragment.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
